planting.note: Move outdoors into a sheltered, humid shade bed only after nights stay reliably above 55F.

directions: Grow this Himalayan foothill species in a loose, humus-rich mix with steady moisture and high ambient humidity. Its dusky blue-green and chocolate-mottled leaves color best under bright, filtered shade rather than direct sun. Divide crowded rhizome clumps in spring to refresh vigor and propagate new plants. Keep it above roughly 55F year-round since it has no frost tolerance.
sources: Kew Plants of the World Online

planting.note: Best kept in terrarium or greenhouse conditions; only set outside in deep, sheltered shade once warm and humid.

directions: This Sarawak rainforest rhizomatous species forms a low creeping mat, with nearly black leaves marked by irregular lime-green spots that give it its name. It needs consistently high humidity and gentle, dappled shade to prevent leaf scorch, making it well suited to terrarium or closed-case culture. Let the rhizome trail across the medium surface and trim rooted sections to propagate. Avoid letting the planting medium dry out fully between waterings.
sources: Kew Plants of the World Online

planting.note: Grow in humid, shaded containers or terrariums; this species has no cold tolerance.

directions: Native to shaded forest floors of southern China, Laos, and Vietnam, this low spreading rhizomatous species carries asymmetrical, fringed leaves with silvery bands and dark veining. It does best with elevated humidity and bright, indirect shade, and resents prolonged dryness at the roots. Whole leaves or leaf sections root readily, making propagation straightforward. Keep temperatures above about 50F to avoid cold damage.

planting.note: Set out after frost danger passes; grows well in large containers moved outdoors for summer.

directions: A cane-stemmed species from the hills above Rio de Janeiro, this begonia produces glossy foliage and loose clusters of bright orange flowers over a long season. It performs best with bright, filtered light rather than deep shade, which encourages sturdier canes and more bloom. Pinch young stems to build a bushier plant and take stem cuttings to propagate. Bring potted specimens indoors well before frost, since it has no cold hardiness.
sources: Kew Plants of the World Online

planting.note: Best as a hanging or trailing shade plant moved outdoors only in warm, humid weather.

directions: Found on the shaded floor of Brazil's Atlantic Forest, this species carries unusually large soft leaves and clusters of white flowers with a yellow center that turn fragrant in spring. It suits hanging baskets or trailing display in bright shade with consistently high humidity. Stem cuttings root easily in a humid propagation chamber. Protect it from drafts and keep it above roughly 60F, since cold quickly damages the foliage.
